prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose standard companion presets or create a custom pet from your photos."]
1: ["Existing Owner or New Companion?", "If you already created a pet before, select restore so your pet is not overwritten.", "Restore Existing Pet", "Create New Pet Account"]
2: ["Name Your Desktop Companion", "Confirm your pet's name to complete the adoption process.", "Pet Name", "Official Pet Adoption Certificate"]
3: ["Select Desktop Home Position", "Pick which corner of your screen your pet should stay near when idle.", "Screen Corner"]
4: ["Use the exact email address from your purchase to preserve existing pet saves."]
5: ["Estimated wait: ~60s", "1. Building 3D model\\n2. Animating behaviors\\n3. Spawning on desktop"]
6: ["For best results, upload clear front-facing photos with good lighting and no heavy filters."]
7: []
8: ["Your Companion is Ready!", "Right-click your pet anywhere on your desktop to hide, chat, or access controls."]
9: ["Select Companion Personality", "Compare companion traits side-by-side to find the right fit for your desktop."]

verdicts.problem: Mentions a purchase and asks for the user's personal email address.
